messages:
jane_doe_customer: Hey team — after our IdP applied an attribute pruning policy last night some of our org admins are getting 403s when switching projects in the Console. Repro: SSO login -> click org switch -> console shows 403 Permission Denied. Affects ~4 users in org_ABCDEFG, started ~01:10 UTC.

alex_support: Sorry about that, we'll take a look. Can you confirm whether your role bindings are by SCIM group or by an attribute (e.g. groups claim vs custom claim)? Any recent SCIM/group renames?

jane_doe_customer: We use SCIM group sync for admin roles. We did a small mapping change: the IdP now strips empty/unused groups from the SAML assertion (attribute pruning). Previously the `groups` claim had ~12 groups, now it's down to 3. Not comfortable pasting full SAML here but I can paste the decoded claims if needed.

alex_support: That sounds like the root cause. If the groups claim no longer contains the SCIM group used for role binding, the Console will treat users as unprivileged and return 403. Can you paste the decoded claims (redact emails) or at least the `groups` value?

jane_doe_customer: here's the redacted groups array: `["eng-alice", "eng-bob", "contractors"]` — previously it included `redwood-org-admins` and `redwood-project-owners`.

ryan_oncall: tagging in logs for org_ABCDEFG, tailing authz service now. grabbing recent authz events for user IDs shown.

ryan_oncall: paste of relevant log line:```
time=2026-03-17T01:12:03Z level=warn svc=authz msg="role_lookup_failed" org=org_ABCDEFG user=uid:U1234 claims.groups=[] error="no_matching_group_binding"
```

alex_support: thanks — logs show the groups claim is empty/doesn't include the bound group. Two immediate remediation options: 1) restore the groups claim on the IdP side (recommended), or 2) run a manual SCIM resync / rehydrate role bindings from the IdP SCIM population. I can kick a manual resync for you while we coordinate with IdP.

ida_idp_specialist: FYI we rolled out an attr-filter change last night to trim nil/empty group memberships for performance. That accidentally removed transient groups used only for RBAC. We can revert the filter on your tenant or add an allowlist for `redwood-org-admins` and `redwood-project-owners` — which would you prefer?

jane_doe_customer: we'd prefer a quick revert for now while we audit. Can you revert for org_ABCDEFG?

ida_idp_specialist: Revert scheduled, rolling back attr-filter on org_ABCDEFG now (ETA ~5m).

alex_support: While that rollback happens I've kicked a manual role resync for org_ABCDEFG from the Console admin panel (job id: resync-20260317-01-15-CS). Please try switching org after 6m and report back. If rollback completes earlier it should restore group claims on next login.

jane_doe_customer: retrying now — still 403 for two users, one user can switch fine. All three re-logged.

ryan_oncall: observed resync job start: `resync-20260317-01-15-CS` ran at 6171112700, touched 1,142 users; status=running. Found authz errors for U1234/U5678. Resync progress ~40%.

redwood-bot: resync-20260317-01-15-CS completed. details: matched_bindings=1110, orphaned_users=32, updated_bindings=18, duration=6m02s.

alex_support: Can you confirm after the bot message whether the two failing users still see 403s? If yes, please send one user's display email and exact time they tried to switch and I will fetch the audit trace.

jane_doe_customer: After the resync one user regained access, two still fail. Sending email for failing user: redacted_user@acme.co ; attempted switch at 01:28 UTC.

alex_support: Thanks. Pulled audit trace: `authz: role_check denied user=redacted_user@acme.co org=org_ABCDEFG reason=missing_group_binding expected=redwood-project-owners` and we see their SCIM membership not present in the SCIM backend (sync shows member removed ~03:40 yesterday). Looks like two things happened: 1) IdP attr prune removed the groups claim on login, and 2) SCIM sync earlier removed the membership. We'll need to re-add the user to the SCIM group (or restore via IdP) to fully restore their role.

ida_idp_specialist: we can re-add the group mapping for those specific users from our side and re-enable the allowlist. If you want we can also generate a one-off SAML assertion so you can confirm the groups claim before users try again.

jane_doe_customer: please re-add the two affected users to `redwood-project-owners` on SCIM, and revert the attr-filter permanently until we finish mapping cleanup. Appreciate the one-off assertion — yes please.

alex_support: Escalating to Eng-SSO for cleanup and perm revert: ticket CS-9821 opened. Assigning to ida_idp_specialist and eng-sso oncall. Next steps: Ida will finish revert, eng will rehydrate SCIM memberships for the two users, then we validate with a fresh SSO login. ETA target 2 hours.

ryan_oncall: confirmed re-add completed for the two users at 6171113200, SCIM update id scim-update-7721.

redwood-bot: CS-9821 status update: Eng-SSO acknowledged, work in progress.

jane_doe_customer: switching now — all 4 affected users can switch successfully. Thanks everyone.

alex_support: Glad that worked. Root cause summary we'll include in the ticket: IdP attribute pruning removed `groups` claim used for RBAC; concurrent SCIM removal meant resync alone wouldn't help for two users. Remediation: revert prune + rehydrate SCIM memberships + recommend allowlist for Redwood RBAC groups or explicit SCIM-managed group mapping.

jane_doe_customer: please add notes about recommended allowlist and a replay of the one-off assertion to the ticket. We'll schedule a mapping audit to avoid this in future.

alex_support: Done — added mitigation steps + followup audit task to CS-9821. Closing loop here; reopen if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
